clips.send: The Great Migration. About 1915–1970. Push: Jim Crow segregation laws (种族隔离法), violence, and poor pay as sharecroppers in the South. Pull: factory jobs in Chicago, Detroit, New York, Philadelphia — first in World War I, again in World War II. Black newspapers like the Chicago Defender urged people to come. In the second wave (1940–1970) many went west too: Los Angeles, Oakland and the Bay Area shipyards. It reshaped American cities, music (jazz, blues) and politics — and fed the Harlem Renaissance.
